subject: Week 49: start bottle weaning now — whole milk arrives at 12 months
bodyText:
This week
First words besides mama and dada are emerging for some — the CDC checkpoint is 15 months — while comprehension surges: he likely follows simple gesture-plus-word directions now (https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html). Self-feeding sharpens as the mastered pincer grasp meets early utensil experiments; expect messy but determined spoon work. Cruising, momentary standing, and first steps for some — the wide 9–15+ month walking range holds, and no action is needed either way before the 15-month checkpoint.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Cup or milk refusal in the first days of a bottle swap — acceptance often takes 10+ exposures; keep offering without pressure.
- [low concern] Frustration bursts when a desired object is blocked — toddler-tantrum precursors, on schedule.
- [monitor] Refusal of every milk substitute for more than a week, or weight stagnation across the transition.
- [call within 24h] Sharply reduced intake with noticeably fewer wet diapers.
- [call now] Choking with no air movement, cough, or cry — start back blows and call 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Swap one mid-morning or mid-afternoon bottle for a snack plus milk in a cup this week, then drop roughly one bottle per week — daytime bottles first, the pre-bed bottle last and decoupled from the sleep routine. AAP targets full bottle weaning by 12–18 months; prolonged bottle use tracks with iron deficiency and dental caries.
- Practice the open cup at every high-chair meal — a small cup, an ounce of water, your hand steadying his. Drinking from a lidless cup as you hold it is a 12-month CDC milestone, and open-cup skill is the developmental target the sippy cup only postpones. CDC 12-month milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
- Play one-step direction games on a daily walk to a familiar destination — say give me the leaf while pointing, then fade the gesture over the week. Following gesture-plus-word directions is the 15-month CDC checkpoint, and comprehension practice now feeds expressive language later. CDC 15-month milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
- Order the smash cake from a local bakery now — lead time runs 2–3 weeks and the birthday is under 4 weeks out. A fruit alternative (stacked watermelon rounds with whipped cream) photographs the same with less sugar, if you want to keep year one nearly sugar-free.

Upcoming
- Day 364–380 (May 10–26, 2027): 12-month well visit — confirm the booking; MMR #1, VAR #1, HepA #1, PCV #4, Hib booster, hemoglobin, and lead screen all land here.
- Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday — bakery cake orders effectively close this week; finalize the guest list alongside.
- By Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit — book now if it is not on the calendar; the AAP by-age-1 window closes with the birthday.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Shows you an object she likes
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Joint attention with intention to share — distinct from pointing to request. Strong autism-screen marker when consistently absent.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/shows-object-she-likes/complete

- Follows directions given with a gesture and words
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Combined verbal + nonverbal cues. Pure-verbal compliance comes after.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/follows-gesture-plus-words/complete

- Copies other children while playing
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Peer-directed imitation, not just imitation of parents.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/copies-other-children/complete

- Hugs a stuffed doll or other toy
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Pretend nurture — early symbolic play. Often emerges with a favorite lovey.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hugs-stuffed-toy/complete

- Stacks at least two small objects (like blocks)
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Visuomotor coordination + planning. Knocking the stack down is also part of the practice.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/stacks-two-objects/complete
